static_traits.name: Lin Qing
static_traits.medical_history: Have not received psychotherapy before; no significant physical illness; no prior reports of similar problems
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, able to identify and describe my feelings and thought patterns; Positive attitude, but with self-reproach and rumination tendencies

basic_info.main_problem: At a weekend chess event, overall successful and rewarding, but because of a small episode of spilling water on oneself during a match, feeling frustrated, tending to ignore the positive side and over-focus on that negative event, causing the positive experience to be overshadowed.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to address my tendency to 'negate the positive and over-focus on the negative', improving overall mindset and enjoyment of activities.

special_situations.event: At a weekend chess tournament, spilled water on himself and was seen by bystanders
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make a mistake or lose face in front of everyone, the whole activity counts as failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly Reflecting after events and focusing on mistakes, downplaying or ignoring positive gains, using self-monitoring to avoid future mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This mistake ruined my whole weekend; everyone was watching me, so embarrassing

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one negative detail appears, it is more important than all positive results
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reviewing in a fault-finding way, only recording and talking about the negative parts
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Victories and Learning do not count; the point is I spilled the water

special_situations.event: When things do not go as planned or minor inconveniences occur (like small mishaps in a race)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If things have not gone as planned, it means I performed poorly
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-reproaches and repeatedly thinks about how to avoid mistakes, reducing attention to positive experiences

positive_force: Invested in and passionate about chess, able to play against strong opponents and win games
Has learning ability and growth willingness (self-describes 'learned a lot')
Able to notice and express one's own emotions and thought patterns (can describe oneself focusing on the negative)
Has motivation to change (actively seeks counseling)
negative_force: Marked cognitive biases: negating the positive, mental filtering, catastrophizing
Highly sensitive to embarrassment, tends to view small mistakes as overall failure
Obvious rumination tendency: repeatedly recalls mistakes and reproaches himself, reducing enjoyment of activities

target_behavior.behavior: Over-focusing on the negative and ruminating after small setbacks, causing Low mood and reduced enjoyment of activities
antecedent: A small accident in a chess competition (spilled water on oneself)
When things do not go as planned or inconveniences occur
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive distortions (mental filtering, negating the positive, catastrophizing) triggering shame/embarrassment, trying to correct mistakes and avoid repeats through rumination
target_behavior.function: Trying to gain a sense of control through Self-monitoring and rumination, avoiding future mistakes; briefly avoiding directly facing embarrassment
target_behavior.consequence: The overall experience is covered by negativity, enjoyment of the activity declines, mood is low, and it may affect communication with others
